chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
One of the two عليهما السلام was asked about a man who enters Makkah after the morning prayer or after the ʿaṣr prayer,
He عليه السلام said: He performs tawaf and prays the two rakʿahs so long as it is not at sunrise or at the time of its reddening.

Thus, the correct approach regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyyah, because that accords with the position of the generality. As for the last report, it is possible to interpret it as referring to the two rakʿahs of supererogatory tawaf, for that is disliked during these two times according to what most narrations indicate. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity, used here in reconciling the reports
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs prayed in connection with tawaf
key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: the ʿaṣr prayer time, another time mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer time, after which the case in question occurs
key_terms.طَوَافِ النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory tawaf, whose two rakʿahs are discussed separately
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city entered for tawaf
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: disliked, indicating a non-preferred legal status at those times
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: he performs tawaf around the Kaʿbah

ai.seo_question: Can the two rakʿahs of tawaf be prayed after the morning or ʿaṣr prayer when entering Makkah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on performing the two rakʿahs of tawaf for one who enters Makkah after the morning or ʿaṣr prayer. It also preserves the compiler’s reconciliation of the reports, explaining some as issued under taqiyyah and others as applying to the two rakʿahs of supererogatory tawaf, which are regarded as disliked at certain times.
